proposed_comments.title: Add provider-mapping coverage for Anthropic
proposed_comments.body:
### Add provider-mapping coverage for Anthropic

**Severity:** `medium`

**Affected code:**
- `src\modules\AdvancedPaste\AdvancedPaste\Services\CustomActions\PasteAIProviderFactory.cs` — provider dispatch.
- `src\modules\AdvancedPaste\AdvancedPaste\Services\CustomActions\AnthropicPasteProvider.cs` — Anthropic request configuration.
- `src\modules\AdvancedPaste\AdvancedPaste.UnitTests` — provider factory and configuration tests.

**Problem:** The new Anthropic service type is registered and dispatched through several layers, but the PR does not add focused tests for that mapping.

**Why it matters:** A regression in the registry, factory, or configuration transfer can leave Anthropic visible in settings while provider creation or request execution silently uses incorrect endpoint or model values.

**Suggested change:**
1. Add a factory test that selects `AIServiceType.Anthropic` and asserts that `PasteAIProviderFactory` returns `AnthropicPasteProvider`.
2. Add a configuration test that supplies a custom Anthropic endpoint and model, then asserts that the provider receives the same values when building its client and request.
3. Cover the default-model fallback so an empty model selection resolves to the intended Anthropic default.

**Verification:** Run the focused `AdvancedPaste.UnitTests` provider-factory and Anthropic-provider tests, including custom endpoint/model and default-model fallback cases.

proposed_comments.title: Cover enterprise-policy enforcement at execution time
proposed_comments.body:
### Cover enterprise-policy enforcement at execution time

**Severity:** `high`

**Affected code:**
- `src\modules\AdvancedPaste\AdvancedPaste\Services\CustomActions\CustomActionTransformService.cs` — execution-time provider policy enforcement.
- `src\modules\AdvancedPaste\AdvancedPaste\Services\CustomActions\PasteAIProviderFactory.cs` — provider resolution.
- `src\modules\AdvancedPaste\AdvancedPaste.UnitTests` — custom-action and policy regression tests.

**Problem:** Anthropic is filtered in settings, but the new execution-time policy path is not covered for saved actions or already-configured providers that still reference Anthropic.

**Why it matters:** Enterprise policy must block the outbound request even when a stale configuration bypasses the settings UI; otherwise a disabled provider can remain configured and attempt to execute.

**Suggested change:**
1. Configure an Anthropic provider or saved action, then set `AllowAdvancedPasteAnthropic` to disabled before execution.
2. Invoke `CustomActionTransformService` and assert that it rejects the transform through the expected user-facing failure path.
3. Assert that `AnthropicPasteProvider.ProcessPasteAsync` is not called and no request is sent when the policy blocks the provider.

**Verification:** Run the focused `AdvancedPaste.UnitTests` custom-action policy tests with Anthropic enabled and disabled, and confirm that only the enabled case reaches the provider execution path.
